title: Set up static IP for internet sharing
summary: Assign a static IP address to the network interface connected to the client devices. This is the first step in configuring a Linux machine to share its internet connection.
prerequisites: Identify the interface connected to the client (e.g., eth1, enp2s0)
Identify the interface connected to the internet (e.g., eth0, wlan0)

steps.explain: Bring up the interface connected to the client devices.
steps.cmd: sudo ip link set up dev <CLIENT_INTERFACE>

placeholders.name: CLIENT_INTERFACE
placeholders.description: Name of the network interface connected to the client(s)

steps.explain: Assign a static IP address to the client interface. Use an address from a private range (like 192.168.x.x) that does not conflict with your internet interface's subnet.

placeholders.name: CLIENT_INTERFACE
placeholders.description: Name of the network interface connected to the client(s)

rollback.explain: To undo this, reboot the machine or manually remove the IP address using 'ip addr del' and bring the interface down with 'ip link set down'.

warnings: Ensure the static IP subnet does not overlap with the subnet of your internet-facing interface.
These changes are temporary and will be lost after a reboot unless configured in a network manager.
